newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee closes flat amid low dlr demand.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee closes flat amid low dlr demand.

text.p: The Sri Lankan rupee closed steady against the dollar on Thursday, amid low demand for the US currency and ample supply of it, dealers said.
The rupee closed at its opening level of 58.85 to the dollar, after rising briefly to 58.87, they said.
"There was hardly any trade-backed or speculative demand for dollars. And there were more than enough dollars to fill the little demand we saw," said a foreign bank dealer.
The Central Bank pushed down the dollar-rupee exchange rate by one-quarter of a local cent, fixing buying and selling prices at 58.8288 and 60.0167.
Overnight call money closed at nine percent after opening at around the same levels, with the market well offered, dealers said.
Dealers expect the dollar-rupee exchange rate and overnight call money to remain at current levels in the absence of a big import bill.
